names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 25 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Ορέντιος, Φαρνάκιος, Έρωτας, Φίρμος, Φιρμίνος, Κυριάκος, και Λογγίνος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 24. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученуци Орентије, Фарнакије, Ерос, Фирмос, Фирмин, Кириак и Лонгин“ — Свети is not a rank and the misprinted мученуци is the rank, which `types` already carries; what is left is one of seven bare forenames, all seven in the nominative, with no see, no place and no by-name to break a fold with. The «brother of Orentius» of the display name is the corpus’s own and §10 reserves it. **Copied as printed**: Фирмин, where the Greek page has «Φιρмίνος» and the corpus display name is Firminus. The Serbian form is a syllable shorter and is not lengthened to match it. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` returns no other holder of the gate’s folded key, so there is no fold and no `READ_FOLDS` key is owed.

Read out of the name link behind his place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 24 июня ст. ст., «Фирмин Апсарский, мч.», with the grade word left off. The epithet is the place of his own death as that page gives it, and it is the calendar's own.

feast.note: The same menologion number this folder's serbian row carries; the greek row — and the romanian one where this folder has it — stand on 25 June, which is those calendars' own day for the company and not a second Russian feast. The one life page days.pravoslavie.ru gives the seven brothers, life1387, heads «День памяти: 24 июня» and names no other day; it was read whole. The day line calls them «семи братий», the seven brothers, and enumerates all seven, and this corpus keeps seven folders, so the company is complete.

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, the fifth of the seven. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. **A COMPANY OF SEVEN, ENUMERATED, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM ALREADY A FOLDER.** The heading prints seven bare forenames under one rank word, „Свети мученуци Орентије, Фарнакије, Ерос, Фирмос, Фирмин, Кириак и Лонгин“, and the corpus holds all seven: `orentius-the-martyr`, `pharnacius-brother-of-orentius`, `eros-brother-of-orentius`, `firmus-brother-of-orentius`, `firminus-brother-of-orentius`, `cyriacus-brother-of-orentius` and `longinus-brother-of-orentius`. §5 counts what the heading enumerates, which is seven, and the body adds nobody: „Рођена браћа.“, brothers by birth, and „Без обзира на њихове војничке заслуге, беху осуђени на прогонство у Каспијске пределе, но успут свих 7, један за другим, од глади и мука скончаше свој живот и преселише се у Царство Христово.“ puts the number at seven again in figures. The heading is quoted **whole** on all seven, as §4 requires, **including its misprint**: it reads мученуци where the word is мученици, and a reader does not mend a source. None of the seven was found by `sr-namesweep.mjs`, which scores only the first name of a company; `ls saints | grep -iE` on the seven stems found all of them at once, the grep beating the sweep again. **THE SERBIAN DAY IS A DAY EARLIER THAN THE OTHER TWO CALENDARS’, AND THAT IS NOT A SECOND DAY.** The corpus keeps these seven on the **25 June** of the Romanian and Greek calendars; this book keeps them on the Julian **24 June**. An attestation is per church and carries that church’s own feast, so the Serbian row is written on 24/6 and no §4 note is owed: a different calendar’s day is not a second day. **And the Prologue does not keep them twice**, which was measured rather than assumed: its Julian 25 June prints two entries, a venerable woman martyr and a venerable Dionysius, and neither is this company — so the rule that two commemorations on one calendar mean two men is not in play, and these are the same seven men the Greek page keeps a day later. **`dates` STAYS NULL ON ALL SEVEN, AND NOW FOR TWO REASONS.** This book dates them only „Беху римски војници у време цара Максимијана.“, they were Roman soldiers in the time of the emperor Maximian, and an emperor is no source for a year and a reign is not a date. **And the two books do not even agree on the emperor**: saint.gr, whose account is in these folders’ own prose, puts them in Thrace in the years of **Diocletian** and dates that to 301 — a year the folders have cited and never recorded, which `date-citation-audit.mjs` prints and which is named for the author here as it was on 23 June. Diocletian and Maximian reigned together, so the two sentences are not in contradiction; neither is a source for a year, and nothing is written from either. `dates` null before and after on every one of the seven. **`types` UNTOUCHED, AND THE CORPUS IS ALREADY UNEVEN HERE IN A WAY THIS BOOK DOES NOT LET A READER FIX.** The heading gives Свети, not a rank, and the misprinted мученуци, which is the `martyr` all seven carry, and nothing else. „Беху римски војници у време цара Максимијана.“ is in the **body**, so `soldier` is refused on the standing rule that a rank inferred from a verb in the body is not written. **Measured, and worth the author’s eye: six of the seven already carry `soldier` and `orentius-the-martyr` does not**, because his folder was made off a bare Romanian line that named no soldiering and the other six off the Greek page that did. The unevenness is the corpus’s own and predates this reading; adding `soldier` to him off this body would be writing a heading rank out of a narrative, so it is named and left. **FOUR THINGS THIS BOOK AND THE GREEK PAGE DISAGREE ON, AND ALL FOUR ARE WRITTEN.** The emperor, as above: Maximian here, Diocletian there. The war: „Када Римљани ратоваху против Скита за Дунавом, свети Орентије изађе на мегдан скитском голијату Мароту и уби га.“ has the Romans warring against the Scythians **beyond the Danube**, where saint.gr has the seven soldiering in **Thrace**. The champion Orentius killed in single combat: this book calls him the Scythian goliath **Марот**, Marot, where saint.gr has **Mararon**; `grep -ril marot saints/` returned nothing before this batch, so the name is new to the corpus. And the exile: „Без обзира на њихове војничке заслуге, беху осуђени на прогонство у Каспијске пределе, но успут свих 7, један за другим, од глади и мука скончаше свој живот и преселише се у Царство Христово.“ sends them to the **Caspian regions** and has all seven end their lives one after another of hunger and torments, where saint.gr sends them to **Armenia** and has them die one after another of the hardships. Both are written in each life and neither is chosen. What the two books agree on is the shape: brothers, soldiers, a duel won, a sacrifice refused, military merit that did not save them, exile, and seven deaths one after another. „Због тога сва римска војска приношаше жртве боговима, али Орентије са браћом изјави, да су они хришћани и да не могу приносити жртве глувим и немим идолима.“ is this book’s refusal — they declared they were Christians and could not offer sacrifice to deaf and dumb idols. **NO ROWS ADDED**: all forty-two reciprocals among the seven are already in place in both directions and this book confirms them; Marot is nobody’s folder, and an emperor takes no row. **No `locations`**: the Danube, the Caspian regions and Scythia are named in clauses. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse, and this day also carries a poem, which is not a hymn either and is dealt with on the second entry. THE VERSE IS NOT USED. The ПЕСМА for 24 June is twenty lines on the Forerunner alone and nothing on the bishop or the seven brothers: it has the knife of Herod miss the child and not miss the child’s father, has angels for the orphan’s shepherds and guardians, and calls him the end of the great prophets and the beginning of God’s apostles. It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not an entry’s account, so §3 of this wave’s brief puts it in no field and in no life, and it is recorded here instead. **For the second day running the verse treats one entry of three or four and ignores the rest**, which is worth the line: the verse is no index of what a day holds.
